thread.title: Warren Buffett: What To Expect From Annual Berkshire Hathaway Letter

author: APARNA NARAYANAN
title: Warren Buffett: What To Expect From Annual Berkshire Hathaway Letter
text:
Warren Buffett lords over an empire that sells everything from candy to car insurance. And on Saturday, the Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKB ) chief releases his hotly awaited annual letter to shareholders.
X Investors in Berkshire Hathaway will look to learn what the Nebraska-based conglomerate will do with a rapidly swelling pile of cash that crossed $100 billion last September. They hope, too, for the 87-year-old chief to drop more clues on a succession plan .
Buffett's letter to shareholders, combining insights from the legendary investor with humorous reflections, has appeared with clockwork regularity every year since 1977. They're archived on the Berkshire Hathaway website .
Some Berkshire watchers are hoping the company will put its cash to use by expanding its portfolio of companies. Berkshire hasn't made a major purchase since its $37 billion acquisition of Precision Castparts, a maker of parts for jet engines and gas turbines, in 2015.
CFRA analyst Cathy Seifert says Berkshire's acquisition strategy is less likely to focus on heavily regulated industries (like those in the financial services sector) when it can leverage upside to these industries via stock investments. Similarly, its technology exposure has been a result of investments, not acquisitions, she added.
"Against that backdrop, our sense is future acquisitions will likely be in the energy, materials and industrials areas, and possibly health care and consumer staples," she wrote in a note Thursday, without naming specific companies.
It's a different story on Buffett's stock buys. Buffett started purchasing Apple ( AAPL ) in 2016 and has steadily raised his stake in the iPhone maker's stock, which has jumped 25% in the past year alone. Apple is now Berkshire's largest stock holding , accounting for roughly 15% of his $191.2 billion portfolio at the end of 2017.
Seifert is also watching for these items in the chairman's letter:
signs of the direction and scale of Berkshire's new health care initiative thoughts and a strategy on the disruptive impact to the auto insurance model from autonomous vehicles any change in company strategy as traditional reinsurers, like those under the Berkshire's umbrella, compete with alternative risk-transfer mechanisms, such as insurance-linked securities or catastrophe bonds Class B shares of Berkshire Hathaway rose 1% to close at 202.76 on the stock market today .
